scenario: You have drafted an outline with six sections. One of them, 'Background', you included out of habit — you cannot say what it establishes that the other sections do not.
expect: Cuts the section rather than keeping it with a vague purpose sentence
Verifies every remaining section has a purpose sentence that names a distinct contribution
Does not pad the outline to reach a section count
Keeps the angle intact after the cut

scenario: The brief names the audience as non-technical executives, but the topic (database index selection) pulls naturally toward implementation detail.
expect: Holds the outline to the stated executive audience rather than drifting technical
Frames each section around decisions and consequences rather than mechanics
Records any technical detail that must survive as a gap needing plain-language framing
Does not substitute a different audience because it fits the topic better
